## Agentic AI {.center}

From tool-using LLMs to autonomous AI systems

> "I think AI agent workflows will drive massive AI progress this year -- perhaps even more than the next generation of foundation models." -- Andrew Ng, 2024

---

## What is Agentic AI?

- **Agentic AI**: An autonomous AI system that can act independently to achieve pre-determined goals
- The term **"agentic"** emphasizes **agency** -- the capacity for independent, goal-driven action
- Unlike traditional AI that requires step-by-step guidance, agentic systems are **proactive** and perform complex tasks with minimal human oversight

> Source: [AWS -- What is Agentic AI?](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/agentic-ai/)

---

## Four Characteristics of Agentic AI

| Characteristic | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| **Proactive** | Anticipates needs, identifies patterns, takes initiative before issues escalate |
| **Adaptable** | Adjusts actions based on real-time input and domain-specific context |
| **Collaborative** | Works alongside humans and other AI agents, accepts human oversight |
| **Specialized** | Multiple hyperspecialized agents, each focused on narrow expertise areas |

> Source: [AWS -- What is Agentic AI?](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/agentic-ai/)

---

## Agentic AI Infrastructure Primitives {.center}

The building blocks for creating, deploying, and operating AI agents

---

## Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Primitives

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides the foundational infrastructure for building agents at scale:

| Primitive | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| **Runtime** | Serverless agent deployment with session isolation |
| **Gateway** | Converts APIs and Lambda functions into agent-compatible tools |
| **Memory** | Maintains context across interactions |
| **Identity** | Secure access management and authentication |
| **Observability** | CloudWatch-powered monitoring, latency, token usage |
| **Policy** | Real-time enforcement of agent action boundaries |
| **Code Interpreter** | Execute code for programmatic tasks and visualizations |

> Source: [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/)

---

## Why These Primitives Matter

- **Tool Use**: Agents need to call external APIs, databases, and services
- **Memory**: Context must persist across turns and sessions
- **Identity**: Agents act on behalf of users and need proper credentials
- **Observability**: You must monitor agent behavior, costs, and errors
- **Guardrails/Policy**: Agents need boundaries to prevent harmful or unintended actions
- **Runtime**: Agents need infrastructure that can handle long-running, stateful sessions

These primitives apply regardless of which agent framework you choose.

## The Progression to Agents

![Progression to agents](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:1100/format:webp/0*5dWPE7IUOXB2f6ap.png)

Source: [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/pt-br/library/resources/ai-agents)

## From Prompting to Agents

1. **Simple Prompting**: Send a question, get an answer (no external data)
2. **In-Context Learning**: Provide examples in the prompt for better responses
3. **RAG**: Retrieve relevant documents to augment the prompt
4. **Tool Use**: LLM can call functions to interact with external systems
5. **Agents**: LLM autonomously decides which tools to use, in what order, and iterates until the task is complete

Each step builds on the previous -- agents represent the most capable pattern.

---

## Anthropic's Definition of Agents {.center}

"LLMs using tools based on environmental feedback in a loop"

---

## The Augmented LLM

The foundation of any agentic system is the **augmented LLM** -- an LLM enhanced with:

- **Retrieval**: Generating search queries and pulling relevant information
- **Tools**: Selecting and invoking appropriate functions
- **Memory**: Determining what information to retain across interactions

> "Our current models can actively use these capabilities -- generating their own search queries, selecting appropriate tools, and determining what information to retain."

Source: [Anthropic -- Building Effective Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

---

## Workflows vs. Agents

Anthropic distinguishes between two types of agentic systems:

### Workflows
- LLMs and tools orchestrated through **predefined code paths**
- Developer defines the sequence of steps
- Offer **predictability and consistency**

### Agents
- LLMs **dynamically direct their own processes** and tool usage
- The model decides the sequence of steps at runtime
- Suited for **open-ended problems** where the number of steps is unpredictable

> **Key insight**: "Start simple. Many patterns can be implemented in a few lines of code."

---

## When to Use Agents vs. Workflows

- Use **workflows** when tasks are well-defined and predictable
- Use **agents** when "it's difficult or impossible to predict the required number of steps, and where you can't hardcode a fixed path"
- **Start with the simplest solution** -- add agentic complexity only when needed
- A direct LLM API call is often sufficient before reaching for a framework

Source: [Anthropic -- Building Effective Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

---

## The Agentic Loop

At its core, an agent is an LLM running in a loop:

```
while not task_complete:
    1. Observe: Receive input or environmental feedback
    2. Think:  Reason about the current state and goal
    3. Act:    Select and invoke a tool (or respond)
    4. Reflect: Evaluate the result
```

This is why Anthropic defines an agent as **"tool use in a loop"** -- the LLM keeps iterating until it determines the task is complete.

---

## AWS Four-Stage Agentic AI Pathway {.center}

Perceive, Reason, Act, Learn

---

## Perceive and Reason

### Perceive
- Agents collect **real-time data** from diverse sources via APIs, services, and applications
- Process structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data
- Determine **relevance** of information to current tasks

### Reason
- LLMs interpret context and develop **action plans**
- Employ **semantic reasoning** and error handling
- Leverage long-term memory for consistency
- Adapt plans using new information received during execution

---

## Act and Learn

### Act
- Execute actions via plugins and integrations with external software
- Perform subtasks **sequentially** -- from API calls to code execution
- **Human-in-the-loop** verification can gate certain actions for safety

### Learn
- Reinforcement learning techniques refine actions based on task success
- Systems learn from autonomous feedback, LLMs, or human input
- Track metrics like latency, confidence, and success rates for continuous improvement

> Source: [AWS -- What is Agentic AI?](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/agentic-ai/)

---

## Agentic Design Patterns {.center}

Five workflow patterns from Anthropic's "Building Effective Agents"

---

## Pattern 1: Prompt Chaining

- **What**: Decompose a task into a **sequence of LLM calls**, where each step processes the output of the previous one
- **How**: Add **programmatic validation gates** between steps to check quality before proceeding
- **When to use**: Tasks that can be cleanly decomposed into fixed subtasks
- **Example**: Generate a document outline, then write each section, then edit for consistency

```
[LLM Call 1] → Gate → [LLM Call 2] → Gate → [LLM Call 3]
```

---

## Pattern 2: Routing

- **What**: **Classify** an input and direct it to a specialized downstream handler
- **How**: An LLM (or classifier) examines the input and selects the appropriate path
- **When to use**: Complex tasks where different categories need fundamentally different approaches
- **Example**: Customer support -- route billing questions to finance, technical issues to engineering, general inquiries to FAQ

```
                    ┌→ [Handler A]
[Classifier LLM] → ├→ [Handler B]
                    └→ [Handler C]
```

---

## Pattern 3: Parallelization

Two variants of running LLM calls simultaneously:

### Sectioning
- Split a task into **independent subtasks** that run in parallel
- Example: Analyze sentiment, extract entities, and summarize -- all at once

### Voting
- Run the **same task multiple times** for higher confidence
- Aggregate results (majority vote, best-of-N)
- Example: Code review from three independent LLM passes

```
         ┌→ [LLM Call A] →┐
Input →  ├→ [LLM Call B] →├→ Aggregate
         └→ [LLM Call C] →┘
```

---

## Pattern 4: Orchestrator-Workers

- **What**: A central **orchestrator LLM** dynamically breaks down tasks and delegates to **worker LLMs**
- **How**: The orchestrator analyzes the input, creates a plan, assigns subtasks to workers, and synthesizes results
- **When to use**: Complex tasks where subtasks cannot be predicted in advance
- **Example**: A coding agent that plans a feature, delegates file edits to workers, then reviews the result

```
                   ┌→ [Worker A] →┐
[Orchestrator] →   ├→ [Worker B] →├→ [Synthesizer]
                   └→ [Worker C] →┘
```

---

## Pattern 5: Evaluator-Optimizer

- **What**: One LLM **generates** a response, another LLM **evaluates** and provides feedback in a loop
- **How**: The generator improves its output based on evaluator feedback until quality criteria are met
- **When to use**: Tasks with clear evaluation criteria where iterative refinement adds value
- **Example**: Code generation where an evaluator checks for bugs and style, and the generator refines

```
[Generator] → [Evaluator] → feedback → [Generator] → ... → Done
```

---

## Choosing the Right Pattern

| Pattern | Predictability | Complexity | Best For |
|---------|---------------|------------|----------|
| **Prompt Chaining** | High | Low | Sequential, well-defined tasks |
| **Routing** | High | Low | Multi-category classification |
| **Parallelization** | High | Medium | Independent subtasks or consensus |
| **Orchestrator-Workers** | Medium | High | Dynamic task decomposition |
| **Evaluator-Optimizer** | Medium | High | Quality-critical iterative tasks |
| **Full Agent** | Low | Highest | Open-ended, unpredictable tasks |

> Start simple and move to more complex patterns only when needed.

---

## Agentic RAG {.center}

When retrieval becomes an agent capability, not just a pipeline step

---

## What is Agentic RAG?

**Traditional RAG**: A fixed pipeline -- query → retrieve → generate

**Agentic RAG**: The agent **decides** when and how to retrieve information

Key differences:

- **Query Routing**: Agent selects the right data source for each query
- **Query Reformulation**: Agent rewrites queries for better retrieval
- **Self-Reflection**: Agent evaluates retrieved results and decides if they are sufficient
- **Iterative Retrieval**: Agent performs multiple rounds of retrieval, refining each time
- **Tool-Augmented Retrieval**: Agent combines retrieval with other tools (calculators, APIs, code execution)

---

## Agentic RAG Patterns

### Adaptive Retrieval
- Agent decides **whether retrieval is needed** at all (some queries can be answered from LLM knowledge)

### Multi-Source Routing
- Agent selects from **multiple knowledge bases** (vector DB, SQL database, web search, APIs)

### Iterative Refinement
- Agent retrieves → evaluates quality → reformulates query → retrieves again
- Continues until the answer meets quality threshold

### Corrective RAG (CRAG)
- Agent grades retrieved documents for relevance
- Triggers web search or alternative sources when retrieval quality is low

---

## Agentic RAG vs. Traditional RAG

| Aspect | Traditional RAG | Agentic RAG |
|--------|----------------|-------------|
| **Retrieval** | Fixed pipeline, always retrieves | Agent decides when to retrieve |
| **Query** | User query passed as-is | Agent reformulates for better results |
| **Sources** | Single knowledge base | Multiple sources, dynamically selected |
| **Evaluation** | No self-assessment | Agent evaluates result quality |
| **Iteration** | Single pass | Multiple rounds until satisfied |
| **Tools** | Retrieval only | Retrieval + code execution + APIs |

---

## Agent Frameworks Landscape {.center}

Open-source frameworks and managed services for building agents (2025-2026)

---

## Agent Frameworks Overview

The agent framework ecosystem has matured significantly:

| Framework | Provider | Key Approach | License |
|-----------|----------|--------------|---------|
| **LangGraph** | LangChain | Graph-based state machines | MIT |
| **Strands Agents** | AWS | Model-driven, minimal code | Apache 2.0 |
| **Claude Agent SDK** | Anthropic | Built on Claude Code | MIT |
| **Agents SDK** | OpenAI | Minimal primitives, handoffs | MIT |
| **Agent Development Kit** | Google | Code-first, Gemini-optimized | Apache 2.0 |
| **Bedrock AgentCore** | AWS | Managed infrastructure | Managed service |

---

## LangGraph

**Graph-based agent orchestration** from LangChain

- Agents defined as **state machines** with nodes (computation) and edges (transitions)
- **Explicit state management** throughout execution -- deterministic, traceable
- **Human-in-the-loop**: Built-in statefulness for review and approval workflows
- **Memory**: Conversation histories persist across sessions
- **Streaming**: Token-by-token output with intermediate step visualization
- Supports single-agent, multi-agent, hierarchical, and sequential architectures

```python
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph

graph = StateGraph(AgentState)
graph.add_node("agent", call_model)
graph.add_node("tools", tool_node)
graph.add_edge("agent", "tools")
```

> Source: [LangGraph](https://www.langchain.com/langgraph)

---

## AWS Strands Agents SDK

**Model-driven agents in a few lines of code**

- Open-source framework by AWS -- "a model-driven approach to building AI agents"
- **Model-agnostic**: Supports Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, and more
- **Native MCP support**: Integrate any MCP server as agent tools
- **Multi-agent primitives**: Built-in handoffs, swarms, and graph workflows
- Deploys to Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda, EKS, Fargate, and more

```python
from strands import Agent, tool

@tool
def word_count(text: str) -> int:
    """Count words in text."""
    return len(text.split())

agent = Agent(tools=[word_count])
agent("How many words are in this sentence?")
```

> Source: [Strands Agents](https://strandsagents.com/)

---

## Claude Agent SDK

**Build agents with Claude Code** from Anthropic

- Official SDK for building agents powered by Claude
- Two APIs: `query()` for simple async calls, `ClaudeSDKClient` for interactive sessions
- **Custom tools via SDK MCP servers** -- define Python functions as tools without separate processes
- **Hooks system** for programmatic control over agent actions (approve, deny, modify)
- Built-in tools: Read, Write, Bash, and more

```python
from claude_agent_sdk import query
import anyio

async def main():
    async for message in query(prompt="What is 2 + 2?"):
        print(message)

anyio.run(main)
```

> Source: [Claude Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-sdk-python)

---

## OpenAI Agents SDK

**Minimal primitives, maximum flexibility**

- Production-ready evolution of OpenAI's experimental "Swarm" project
- Intentionally minimal design: **Agents**, **Handoffs**, and **Guardrails**
- **Agent loop**: Built-in tool invocation loop with environmental feedback
- **Handoffs**: Agents delegate to specialized agents seamlessly
- **Guardrails**: Parallel validation of inputs and outputs
- Built-in MCP support, sessions for persistent memory, and tracing for debugging

```python
from agents import Agent, Runner

agent = Agent(
    name="assistant",
    instructions="You are a helpful assistant.",
)
result = Runner.run_sync(agent, "Write a haiku about recursion.")
print(result.final_output)
```

> Source: [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/)

---

## Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)

**Code-first Python framework** for sophisticated AI agents

- Optimized for Gemini but **model-agnostic** and **deployment-agnostic**
- **Multi-agent systems**: Define sub-agents with coordinator/child relationships
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol**: Standard for remote agent communication
- Rich tool ecosystem: MCP tools, OpenAPI specs, custom functions
- Built-in development UI for testing, evaluation, and debugging

```python
from google.adk.agents import Agent
from google.adk.tools import google_search

root_agent = Agent(
    name="search_assistant",
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    instruction="Answer questions using Google Search when needed.",
    tools=[google_search]
)
```

> Source: [Google ADK](https://github.com/google/adk-python)

---

## Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

**Managed infrastructure** -- not a framework, but the platform underneath

- **Build**: Persistent memory, secure tool connectivity, code interpreter, secure browser runtime
- **Deploy**: Serverless with session isolation, workloads up to 8 hours, identity provider integration
- **Monitor**: CloudWatch dashboards for token usage, latency, error rates, quality evaluation

### Works with any framework
- Strands Agents, LangGraph, CrewAI, or custom code
- You build the agent logic; AgentCore handles the infrastructure

> Source: [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/)

---

## Multi-Agent Orchestration {.center}

When one agent is not enough

---

## Modern Multi-Agent Architectures

The industry uses two primary multi-agent structures:

### Horizontal Architecture
- Multiple agents with **equal technical proficiency**
- Each specializes narrowly and collaborates **laterally**
- Example: Research agent + coding agent + review agent working as peers

### Vertical Architecture
- **Hierarchical** structure with orchestrator and worker agents
- Higher-level agents handle reasoning and decision-making
- Lower-level agents manage data collection and task execution
- Example: Supervisor agent delegates to specialized sub-agents

> Detailed multi-agent patterns, memory, and state sharing covered in **Week 6**.

---

## Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocol

- **Open protocol** for communication between opaque agentic applications
- Originally contributed by Google, now hosted by the **Linux Foundation**
- **Complementary to MCP**: MCP connects agents to tools and resources; A2A connects agents to other agents
- Agents collaborate **without sharing internal memory, proprietary logic, or tool implementations**
- SDKs available in Python, Go, JavaScript, Java, and .NET
- Supported by Google ADK, Strands Agents, and other frameworks

> Source: [A2A Protocol](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A)

---

## Summary

- **Agentic AI** = autonomous AI systems with agency (proactive, adaptable, collaborative, specialized)
- **Agent primitives**: Tool use, memory, identity, observability, guardrails, runtime
- **Anthropic's definition**: An agent is "LLMs using tools based on environmental feedback in a loop"
- **Workflows vs. Agents**: Use workflows for predictable tasks, agents for open-ended problems
- **Five design patterns**: Prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer
- **Agentic RAG**: Agent-driven retrieval with query routing, self-reflection, and iterative refinement
- **Frameworks**: LangGraph, Strands Agents, Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Bedrock AgentCore
- **Multi-agent**: Horizontal (peer) and vertical (hierarchical) architectures; A2A protocol for cross-agent communication
